findings.description: Direct inspection of all five V187 views and six pose renders: the lower-front UpperLeg weight adjustment is present, but the skirt remains strongly faceted and angular across front, side and rear. In crouch, broad upper-thigh and shorts areas remain visible below the overskirt; in sit, the front lap still separates from the raised thighs and the skirt gathers behind the pelvis. The pose response and coverage remain unacceptable.

The V187 front and side views still show angular planar shading on the bodice and a small gray patch near the waist; the rear waist flap remains stiff. The surface ownership/cause of the waist patch is unverified. Bodice appearance remains unacceptable.

Direct inspection of same-pose V187 renders and depth-tested component-ID renders from the exact weighted mesh (6bc32c7d64f2460d328621deed7b86644d2f66e7f5315af8aaf5313040c9ff66): visible shorts-only pixels at 1024x1024 are 7637 in crouch and 10192 in sit; front-lap pixels are 2382 and 2912. The ID views show the lap occupying a small upper-front patch while thigh surface remains exposed below; these counts are view-dependent projected area, not a fit metric. The existing surface-ray diagnostic remains 402/885 shorts-covered upper-thigh samples per side in crouch, 401/885 in sit, and front-lap union hits of 54/532 and 23/532 respectively. Weight adjustment did not improve coverage; appearance, fit, and release remain rejected/blocked.
